title: Gravimetric verification of a 1000 µL micropipette
summary: Check whether an adjustable air-displacement pipette delivers its nominal volume by weighing replicate deliveries of water, converting mass to volume with a temperature-dependent factor, and comparing the systematic and random errors with acceptance limits.
scenario: A 100–1000 µL pipette is due for its routine check. You have a reservoir of distilled water equilibrated to the room, an analytical balance with a small weighing vessel and a thermometer. Run the check at the nominal volume and complete the verification record.
guided_steps: Measure the temperature of the test water; the mass-to-volume factor depends on it.
Set the pipette to its nominal volume, 1000 µL.
Fit a new tip and pre-wet it by filling and emptying it several times, discarding the water to waste.
Tare the balance with the weighing vessel in place.
Hold the pipette vertical and immerse the tip 2–4 mm below the surface while aspirating.
Dispense against the inside wall of the vessel and finish with a touch-off.
Record the balance reading, tare again, and repeat until you have 10 readings.
Convert each reading to volume with V = m × Z, where Z = (1/(ρ_water − ρ_air)) × (1 − ρ_air/ρ_weights) in µL/mg.
Compute the mean volume, the systematic error (mean − nominal)/nominal × 100 and the random error as a coefficient of variation, s/mean × 100.
Compare both with the acceptance limits and record pass or fail.

source.note: A readability of 0.1 mg is common for checking 1000 µL deliveries; smaller volumes need a finer balance.
Ten replicates per test volume is common practice; the governing method is ISO 8655-6, which was not read for this protocol.
Practice limit for this simulation. A real laboratory takes its limits from its SOP, the manufacturer or ISO 8655-2, which was not read for this protocol.
Practice limit for this simulation; see the systematic limit.

checkpoints.description: Measure the water temperature before converting masses to volumes.
checkpoints.rationale: Water density, and so the factor Z, changes with temperature; near 21 °C it changes by about 0.02% per °C.

checkpoints.description: Test at the nominal volume of the pipette.
checkpoints.rationale: Acceptance limits are stated for a specified test volume; readings at another setting cannot be compared with them.

checkpoints.description: Pre-wet each new tip before its first measured delivery.
checkpoints.rationale: A dry tip and its air cushion take up vapour on the first fill, so the first delivery is low.

checkpoints.description: Immerse the tip 2–4 mm while aspirating.
checkpoints.rationale: Too shallow draws air; too deep leaves liquid on the outside of the tip that is then delivered.

checkpoints.description: Hold the pipette vertical while aspirating.
checkpoints.rationale: Tilting changes the hydrostatic head on the air cushion and the volume drawn.

checkpoints.description: Finish each dispense with a touch-off against the vessel wall.
checkpoints.rationale: Without it the last drop can stay on the tip.

checkpoints.description: Tare before each dispense, or difference successive readings.
checkpoints.rationale: Cumulative readings give the total, not each delivery.

checkpoints.description: Record at least 10 readings at the test volume.
checkpoints.rationale: The random error is a standard deviation; too few replicates estimate it poorly.

checkpoints.description: Report the mean volume computed from your readings with the correct factor Z.
checkpoints.rationale: Mass becomes volume only through the density of water at the measured temperature and the buoyancy of air.

checkpoints.description: Report the systematic error as (mean − nominal)/nominal × 100.
checkpoints.rationale: This is the inaccuracy the acceptance limit is written against.

checkpoints.description: Report the random error as the coefficient of variation, s/mean × 100, using the sample standard deviation.
checkpoints.rationale: This is the imprecision the second limit is written against.

checkpoints.description: Record pass only if both errors are within their limits.
checkpoints.rationale: A pipette that fails either limit must be taken out of use, adjusted or serviced, then re-checked.

sources.use: Water density formula used to compute Z.

limitations: Acceptance limits, immersion depth and replicate count are practice values chosen for this simulation, not limits taken from ISO 8655, which was not read.
Evaporation from the weighing vessel, balance drift and the operator's hand warming the pipette are not modelled.
The simulation cannot train the feel of the plunger stops, which is learned only at a bench.
